## Name 5 signal

* Name 5 topics: `<uuid>` (HIGH, conf 0.88, recurring — 12 customers in 30d) and `<uuid>` (LOW, conf 0.65, new — "green light accounts show no active accounts"). Same underlying symptom, clustered together.

## Why new

No open canonical. The symptom is recurring again at high volume (12 in 30d), indicating a regression or a new manifestation with no ticket tracking it.

relatedSnapshot.title: Password reset emails not delivered to user (accepted by provider, never landing) — <email>
relatedSnapshot.description:
BUG: Unconfirmed (email deliverability issue; the reset flow itself works)

## Evidence

* Customer Name 10 Name 8 (user id `<uuid>`, email `<email>`) cannot log in and never receives the password reset email. Reported via Intercom.
* Prod DB (read-only): account healthy — `email_verified=true`, not banned, credential account with password present. 4 reset-password verification tokens generated today for this user (00:16, 00:19, 01:18, 01:42 UTC), so Name 7 reset flow generates links correctly.
* Axiom: no email-send errors around those timestamps → Resend accepted the sends (no `EmailSendError` thrown).
* The recipient mailbox works and is actively receiving OTHER Acquisity mail (AI SDR escalation notifications, etc.) — see screenshots in the Intercom thread. AI SDR escalation emails go through the same `emailService`/Resend sender (`env.EMAIL_FROM`) as the password reset email, yet the reset email specifically never lands.
* Pattern (provider accepts the send, mail never delivered, to an address that receives our other mail) most strongly suggests the recipient is on Resend's suppression/bounce list. Could not verify directly — no Resend credentials available in the investigation session.

## Second issue found

* CS attempted to change the account email to `<email>`, but the change did NOT persist — `user.email` is still `<email>` and `user.updated_at` is `2026-06-13` (unchanged). So the 'change email + resend' retest actually still sent to `<email>`; `<email>` never received a reset. Needs confirmation whether the admin email-change flow requires user confirmation (by design) or silently failed.

## What's needed to resolve

1. Check Resend suppression/bounce list for `<email>` (and `<email>`); remove suppression if present and resend.
2. Investigate why the admin email change did not persist.
3. Immediate customer unblock (separate from root cause): admin sets a temporary password directly so the user can log in without email.

## Links

* Intercom: <url:app.intercom.com>
* Slack thread: <url:acquisityworkspace.slack.com>
* Name 9 session: <url>
